body: Star Ocean: Till the End of Time is tri-Ace's PlayStation 2 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 27 February 2003. The third main Star Ocean follows Fayt Leingod into a conflict that carries him across worlds with very different levels of technology. Its combination of space travel and local fantasy settings gives the journey several scales, from a small group seeking safety to questions about the universe around them. Exploration and character development lead into battles where the player moves and attacks directly instead of selecting every action from a menu.

A three-person party enters real-time battles, with the player controlling one member and directing the others through tactics or switching characters. Both health and mental points matter: losing either can knock a character out. Special actions also consume resources, so an impressive attack has to be judged against what remains afterwards. The Fury meter adds another rhythm, recovering while the character stays still and limiting continuous movement and action. Choosing when to pause, change position or commit to an attack becomes part of keeping the whole party active.

A Director's Cut followed in Japan in 2004, adding characters, dungeons and other features. North American and European editions used this revised version, making it the form through which many players first encountered the game. Yoshiharu Gotanda directed and co-wrote the adventure, with Motoi Sakuraba supplying its music. The original Japanese edition was among Enix's final releases before the Square Enix merger. Within Star Ocean, it combines the series' active combat and science-fiction premise with a story remembered for the scale of the questions it eventually raises.
